Maritime NDT training in Norfolk: the short answer

Maritime NDT training for Norfolk and Hampton Roads ship-repair employers is delivered by Atlantis NDT as live online classes or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and concentrate on repair work: UT thickness gauging, MT and PT on cracked and repaired structure, VT for surveys, and UT and PAUT on repair welds. Navy repair adds NAVSEA requirements within the employer's programme. Atlantis has no Norfolk training centre; quotes are on request.

Norfolk's waterfront is a repair and maintenance economy rather than a new-construction one. Ships arrive with corrosion, fatigue cracks, damaged plating and worn machinery, and leave after a scheduled availability with every repair weld examined and documented. That changes what a technician needs. New-construction examiners spend their days on fresh welds in clean plate; repair examiners spend theirs on coated, pitted, previously repaired steel, in tanks and voids, on deadlines set by the ship's operational schedule. This page covers that repair angle. For new construction, see maritime NDT training in Newport News.

Ready to plan? Request a maritime NDT training quote for Norfolk.

Ship-repair NDT work in Norfolk and Hampton Roads

Navy surface-ship maintenance

Naval Station Norfolk is the largest naval base in the world, and the ships homeported there go through regular maintenance availabilities. The Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center coordinates much of that work, and private repair yards perform it under NAVSEA's Master Ship Repair Agreement and Agreement for Boat Repair. Private repair contractors in the area include BAE Systems Norfolk Ship Repair, General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk, Colonna's Shipyard, Marine Hydraulics International and Lyon Shipyard, alongside dozens of subcontractors who perform specialist work, including NDT, during availabilities. Navy repair work is specified through NAVSEA Standard Items and work specifications, which call up NAVSEA NDT and acceptance requirements for each repair.

The public yard in Portsmouth

Norfolk Naval Shipyard, despite its name, sits across the Elizabeth River in Portsmouth. It is a Navy-operated public shipyard that maintains and modernises carriers and submarines, including their nuclear propulsion plants. Its examiners are certified under the Navy's own programme. Nuclear scope is covered on our nuclear NDT training page for the Peninsula and nuclear NDT consulting in Norfolk.

Commercial ship repair, tugs, barges and offshore

The commercial side covers tugs, barges, dredges, ferries, government vessels and occasional deep-sea ships repaired to class. Here, classification societies such as ABS set survey requirements, and repair examination answers to class rules and the owner's specification. Hull thickness measurement for class surveys is a specialised service: class societies typically require the measuring firm to be approved for the purpose, and the technicians to be qualified in UT thickness measurement.

The port and waterfront industry

The Port of Virginia's Norfolk International Terminals and the Portsmouth terminals generate inspection work on cranes, lifting gear, mooring structures and terminal equipment, as do the coal, bulk and fuel terminals along the Elizabeth River. Military Sealift Command and Coast Guard assets in Hampton Roads add further government repair scope.

What an availability looks like to an NDT technician

A typical repair availability follows a rhythm. Before and just after arrival, inspection crews open tanks and voids, gauge plating and map cracks so the planners can confirm or grow the work package. During the production phase, examiners check excavations before re-welding, then examine finished repair welds against the acceptance criteria called up by the work item. Near the end, examinations close out the paperwork that lets the ship leave on time. Workload peaks are sharp, and they move with the Navy's schedule, which is why Norfolk employers value technicians certified in several methods who can switch between gauging, MT, PT and UT inside a single shift.

Methods used on ship repair in Norfolk

MethodRepair application in NorfolkCode / standard usually invoked
UT thickness gaugingHull plating, tank boundaries, decks and piping wastage; class survey gauging through coatingsClass rules (ABS and others) for survey gauging; NAVSEA work specifications for Navy ships
UT flaw detectionRepair welds in shell plate and structure, insert plates, shaft and rudder stock examinationsNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 with MIL-STD-2035 acceptance (Navy); class rules or AWS D1.1 (commercial)
PAUTEncoded examination of repair butt welds and critical joints where an auditable record is wantedAs permitted by the work specification
MTCrack detection in ferritic structure, excavation checks before re-welding, final repair welds, foundationsNAVSEA 271 / MIL-STD-2035; ASTM E1444 for technique
PTNon-magnetic materials: copper-nickel and stainless piping, bronze propellers and fittings, aluminium structureNAVSEA 271 / MIL-STD-2035; class rules
VTTank and void inspection, survey of structure, fit-up and final repair weld visualNAVSEA work specifications; class survey requirements
RTPiping repair welds where a permanent image is required; scheduled to clear radiation areas on a crowded shipNAVSEA 271 / MIL-STD-2035; ASME B31 for commercial piping
ETCrack detection through paint on structure and fittings, heat exchanger and condenser tubingProcedure-specific; work specification

Local method spotlight: ultrasonic thickness gauging done properly. Thickness gauging looks simple and is often handed to the least experienced technician on the crew. In repair work it drives decisions worth a great deal of money: which plates get cropped and renewed, whether a tank passes survey, how long an availability lasts. Gauging through coatings, on pitted surfaces and with the right probe and calibration takes trained judgement. Good repair examiners combine thickness gauging with MT and VT, then build into UT flaw detection. Our UT Level II training, MT Level II and PT Level II courses cover those foundations.

ISO 9712Some foreign-flag ownersNot offered. Context only.

In short: a Norfolk repair technician needs SNT-TC-1A certifications that a NAVSEA-compliant employer can build on, and a repair contractor needs a written practice and procedures that survive both a Navy or prime-contractor audit and a class surveyor's review.

The SNT-TC-1A path for a Norfolk ship-repair technician

  1. Employer written practice sets training hours, experience, exams and recertification per method and level, and for Navy repair work references NAVSEA requirements.
  2. Classroom training in each method, typically starting with VT, UT thickness and MT. The training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Documented experience under certified supervision, with records that show repair-specific work: tanks, voids, cracked structure, coated surfaces.
  4. General, specific and practical exams under a Level III, the practical on real specimens.
  5. Vision examination.
  6. Written certification by the employer.
  7. NAVSEA qualification for Navy work, via the employer's programme.
  8. Recertification as the written practice requires.

More background: SNT-TC-1A training and certification and the Level II path.

Radiation licensing, TWIC, base access and confined spaces

Virginia is an NRC Agreement State, so radiography with sealed sources at commercial sites is licensed by the Virginia Department of Health's Radioactive Materials Program, and radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements. Work inside federal installations under exclusive federal jurisdiction can require NRC reciprocity. Radiography aboard a ship in availability usually means barricading spaces and shooting off-shift, so expect irregular hours.

Access requirements often decide who gets hired. Navy piers and bases need base-access credentials. Marine terminals and other MTSA-regulated facilities need TWIC for unescorted access. Ship repair also involves confined and enclosed spaces, so repair employers commonly require confined-space and gas-free awareness under OSHA's shipyard standards, and the marine chemist or competent person's certificate must be in place before anyone enters a tank. None of these are NDT certifications, but each is part of being ready to work on a Norfolk availability.

How Atlantis delivers maritime NDT training to Norfolk crews

  • Onsite at your facility: an ASNT Level III-led cohort at your shop or yard office using your gauges, flaw detectors, yokes and procedures, with practical exams on your specimens.
  • Live online: theory and exam preparation for crews spread across Norfolk, Portsmouth, Chesapeake and the Peninsula. See online NDT training.
  • Blended, around availabilities: theory between ship arrivals, practical sessions when crews are not committed to a hull. We schedule around your availability calendar instead of a public course date.

Repair-specific emphasis on request: gauging through coatings and on pitted plate, crack mapping and excavation checks, PT on copper-nickel and bronze, documenting findings so that a planner can turn them into a work item, and reading NAVSEA work specifications. Ask about onsite training for your Norfolk repair crew. Multi-site programmes run through corporate NDT training, and the marine corporate training page describes sector cohorts.

Written practices and Level III services for Norfolk repair contractors

Repair contractors and NDT subcontractors in Hampton Roads face audits from primes, the Navy's maintenance organisations and class societies, often in the same year. The findings are rarely about technique and usually about documents: written practices that do not match the methods offered, procedures that do not cite the acceptance standard the work specification requires, incomplete experience records and an unclear Level III arrangement.

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A with NAVSEA and class notes: NDT written practice development.
  • Level III services: procedures and technique sheets for thickness gauging, MT, PT and UT on repair work; exam administration; pre-audit records review.
  • Readiness reviews for subcontractors seeking to support MSRA/ABR yards.

Engineering and inspection consulting in the area: maritime NDT consulting in Norfolk, NDT consulting in Norfolk and maritime NDT consulting in Portsmouth, Virginia. To have a reviewer look at your documents, book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator gives trainees 12 NDT methods across five 3D environments, including a welding workshop and a storage tank setting that is useful for practising thickness-gauging logic and coverage. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens. Local entry: Practical NDT Norfolk.

Local options compared

  • Tidewater Community College and other Hampton Roads colleges run welding and maritime trades programmes that feed into repair NDT. Check current catalogues for NDT-specific courses.
  • Brightpoint Community College (formerly John Tyler, near Richmond) has a long-standing NDT curriculum in its engineering technology programmes.
  • Repair yards and NDT subcontractors often train new hires internally under their own written practice, especially for UT thickness and MT.
  • National and maritime-focused training providers run public classes at their own centres or online and advertise Norfolk pages; at least one maritime NDT trainer has announced an expansion into Hampton Roads.
  • Atlantis NDT: employer cohorts, live online and onsite SNT-TC-1A training, plus written practice and Level III services. Not the right choice if you need a third party to issue NAVSEA qualification, which only the employer's programme can do.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content and practical exams and, where your written practice designates Atlantis as an outside agency, exam administration.

Frequently asked questions about maritime NDT training in Norfolk

How do I get into ship-repair NDT in Norfolk?

Most people start with VT, UT thickness gauging and MT under an employer's written practice, then add UT flaw detection. Repair yards and NDT subcontractors hire trainees, and welders and Navy veterans cross over regularly. NAVSEA qualification for Navy work comes through the employer.

Can I take maritime NDT training online in Virginia?

Theory and exam preparation, yes, through live online classes. The practical part needs real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility.

Is UT thickness gauging a separate certification?

Under SNT-TC-1A it is usually handled as a limited UT certification defined in the employer's written practice. For class survey gauging, the class society also approves the measuring firm. Check what your employer and customer require.

What is the Master Ship Repair Agreement?

It is the NAVSEA agreement that qualifies private yards to act as prime contractors for Navy ship repair. MSRA and ABR holders must meet NAVSEA requirements, including for NDT performed by them or their subcontractors.

Does Atlantis training qualify me for NAVSEA repair work?

It provides method training an employer can credit, but NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 qualification is administered within the employer's programme.

Do I need TWIC for NDT work in Norfolk?

For unescorted access to MTSA-regulated marine facilities such as port terminals, yes. Navy bases use separate access credentials. Many Hampton Roads marine employers expect technicians to hold TWIC.

Do I need a radiography licence in Virginia?

Your employer needs a Virginia Department of Health radioactive materials licence, and you must meet the state's radiographer training and certification requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Which NDT method pays off most for repair work?

Ultrasonic testing, from thickness gauging up to flaw detection and phased array, is used on almost every availability. MT and VT are the daily methods. Salary context is in our NDT salary guide.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on the employer's written practice, which sets hours and experience using SNT-TC-1A as the reference. See the training requirements matrix and practise with UT Level 2 practice questions.

What does maritime NDT training cost in Norfolk?

Atlantis quotes on request, based on methods, levels, group size, delivery mode and any written practice or Level III work. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training in Norfolk?

Those programmes generally need an approved school or listed eligible training provider. Atlantis does not claim that status; check provider lists, or ask whether your employer will fund training. Veterans: see veterans transitioning into NDT.

How is Norfolk different from Newport News for NDT work?

Norfolk is mostly repair and maintenance; Newport News is mostly new construction and carrier refuelling. Repair rewards thickness gauging, crack detection and adaptability; new construction rewards volumetric weld examination at volume. See maritime NDT training in Newport News.
